title: Australian TV presenter apologises for drinking before viral Olympics broadcast
content:
An Australian television presenter has apologised after slurring her words on a live Winter Olympic broadcast having “totally misjudged” drinking alcohol before appearing on camera.

Danika Mason was recording a segment for Channel Nine’s Today show from Livigno in the evening when she stumbled over her words and went off topic to “iguanas”, prompting studio host Karl Stefanovic to explain to viewers that “cold weather” can sometimes inhibit speaking.

Mason apologised the next day, saying she “shouldn’t have had a drink” and the “cold, we’ve got altitude, not having had dinner probably didn’t help as well”.

“Literally like the price of coffee over here is actually fine,” she had said the day before. “It’s more the price of coffee in the U.S. that we’re gonna have to get used to.

“I’m not sure about the iguanas, where are we going with that one?”

The Channel Nine reporter completed the rest of her Milano Cortina round-up, including an update on American skier Lindsey Vonn, but was slurring her words.

“I want to take full responsibility, it’s not the standard I set myself,” she said in her live apology on the Thursday edition. “So in saying that, I’m genuinely really sorry and I’m thanking everyone for those messages I’ve received as well.”

Mason was defended by Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, who appeared on Melbourne radio show Nova 100’s Jase & Lauren and said there was “nothing to see here”.

“I’m pro Danika. Good on her,” Albanese said, per news.com.au. “She’s over in Italy… and she would have been tired. It’s the time difference. It would have been having an impact.”
